doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: High school band with Bill Simon and the Louis versus Bix debate
summary: Playing round dances at Morton's Corners, waiting for Bunny's show, and arguing Louis versus Bix with Bill Simon.

bands.name: Rusty Dedrick and Bill Simon's high school band

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I did, but as a writer. He wrote for Down Beat in the early stages, and he became the Record of the Month producer for Reader’s Digest. And when we were kids, literally high school kids, we had a little band, he and I and a couple of others. And we played Saturday night at Morton’s Corners in a place where dances were half round and half square. We were the round thank God. And the job started at a certain time, but I would not leave my house until Bunny’s show was over. Then I would go to the job.
Well I guess they at least could time you, they knew when you were going to arrive anyway, when Bunny played his last note.
When you said the dances were half round and half square, and you played the round part?
Well you know, with the square dances, with the callers and the fiddle and everything. Sure.
But what kind of music were you playing?

Well we played just songs. East of the Sun/West of the Moon or something. You know, whatever songs of the day. And Billy and I used to always argue. I liked Louis, he liked Bix. I liked Louis and Bunny of course, but his boy was Bix. And we traded records back and forth, and it took me a while to really appreciate Bix Beiderbecke. Later, yes. But at that time, you know Louis was so straight ahead you know, that that was for me.
Yeah. He can really grab you. Bix is a little more subtle.
